plan.planning_summary: The objective is to design a broadband anti-reflection (AR) coating for fused silica in air over 450-700 nm, evaluating layer counts from 4 to 10. The design must use materials from {MgF2, SiO2, Al2O3, Ta2O5, TiO2} and meet soft targets of mean reflectance < 0.8% and worst-case < 3% across 0, 30, and 45 degrees for TE/TM polarizations. Robustness against +/- 1 degree angle error and 2 nm thickness tolerance is required. Four routes are proposed: two fixed-topology analyses (4-layer and 10-layer) to establish baseline performance limits and complexity trade-offs, and two optimization routes (starting with 6-layer and 8-layer topologies) to find the best-performing designs within the allowed layer count range. All routes include robustness analysis.

routes.title: Fixed 4-layer analyze known stack route (MgF2/SiO2/Ta2O5)
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A fixed 4-layer MgF2/SiO2/Ta2O5 stack tests whether the proposed optical mechanism can balance the shared spectral targets, total thickness, and manufacturing robustness.
routes.design_principle: Quarter-wave-like impedance matching using alternating high and low index materials. Starting with a low-index material (MgF2 or SiO2) on the substrate is hypothesized to be more robust for wide-angle performance than starting with high-index, based on standard AR design heuristics for glass substrates.
routes.proposed_topology: exactly 4 finite layers from the incident side: MgF2 / SiO2 / Ta2O5 / MgF2
manufacturing_considerations: Independent one-sigma thickness error of 2 nm
Common incidence-angle offset bounded by +/- 1 degree
theory_basis: Standard quarter-wave AR theory suggests that n_layer = sqrt(n_air * n_substrate) minimizes reflection at a single wavelength. For broadband, multiple layers are needed. A 4-layer system offers 4 thickness variables to tune the spectral response.
expected_advantages: Lowest material cost and shortest deposition time among multi-layer options.
Simpler fabrication process reduces risk of interfacial defects.
known_risks: May not achieve <0.8% mean reflectance across the full 450-700 nm band at oblique angles.
High sensitivity to thickness errors due to fewer layers averaging out dispersion effects less effectively than thicker stacks.

routes.title: Fixed 7-layer analyze known stack route (MgF2/TiO2)
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A fixed 7-layer MgF2/TiO2 stack tests whether the proposed optical mechanism can balance the shared spectral targets, total thickness, and manufacturing robustness.
routes.design_principle: Chirped or multi-quarter-wave design using high-index contrast pairs (TiO2/MgF2 or Ta2O5/SiO2). Using the highest available index contrast (TiO2/MgF2) maximizes bandwidth per pair, while SiO2/Ta2O5 offers better mechanical stability. This route tests the TiO2/MgF2 combination for maximum optical performance.
routes.proposed_topology: exactly 7 finite layers from the incident side: MgF2 / TiO2 / MgF2 / TiO2 / MgF2 / TiO2 / MgF2
manufacturing_considerations: Independent one-sigma thickness error of 2 nm
Common incidence-angle offset bounded by +/- 1 degree
theory_basis: Multilayer interference filters rely on constructive/destructive interference. More layers allow for broader bandwidth suppression of reflection. High index contrast allows for fewer periods to achieve the same bandwidth, but here we fix the count to 10 to test the limit of performance vs. complexity.
expected_advantages: Better angular stability due to flatter spectral response.
known_risks: Higher total physical thickness increases deposition time and stress.
Increased sensitivity to cumulative thickness errors; small deviations in many layers can compound.
TiO2 can have higher absorption or stress compared to Ta2O5/SiO2.

routes.title: Fixed 10-layer optimize existing stack route (SiO2/Ta2O5)
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A fixed 10-layer SiO2/Ta2O5 stack tests whether the proposed optical mechanism can balance the shared spectral targets, total thickness, and manufacturing robustness.
routes.design_principle: Global optimization of layer thicknesses for a 10-layer LHLHLH or HLHLHL stack. SiO2 is preferred as the outermost layer for environmental durability. Ta2O5 provides sufficient index contrast without the potential issues of TiO2 (stress/absorption).
routes.proposed_topology: exactly 10 finite layers from the incident side: SiO2 / Ta2O5 / SiO2 / Ta2O5 / SiO2 / Ta2O5 / SiO2 / Ta2O5 / SiO2 / Ta2O5
manufacturing_considerations: Independent one-sigma thickness error of 2 nm
Common incidence-angle offset bounded by +/- 1 degree
theory_basis: Intermediate layer counts allow for finer control over the spectral shape than bilayers/trilayers, enabling better compensation for dispersion and angle-dependent phase shifts. Ta2O5/SiO2 is a standard, robust pairing for visible AR coatings.
expected_advantages: Good compromise between performance and complexity.
Likely to meet all soft objectives if topology is favorable.
known_risks: Topology constraint (starting with SiO2) might not be globally optimal; starting with Ta2O5 could yield better results.
Optimization landscape may have local minima requiring global search strategies.

routes.title: Fixed 6-layer optimize existing stack route (MgF2/TiO2)
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A fixed 6-layer MgF2/TiO2 stack tests whether the proposed optical mechanism can balance the shared spectral targets, total thickness, and manufacturing robustness.
routes.design_principle: Optimization of an 6-layer LHLHLHLH stack. MgF2 is chosen as the low-index material for its very low refractive index (~1.38), maximizing the index step with TiO2 (~2.4-2.5). This maximizes the bandwidth of the stopband/reflection suppression.
routes.proposed_topology: exactly 6 finite layers from the incident side: MgF2 / TiO2 / MgF2 / TiO2 / MgF2 / TiO2
manufacturing_considerations: Independent one-sigma thickness error of 2 nm
Common incidence-angle offset bounded by +/- 1 degree
theory_basis: High index contrast allows for steeper spectral transitions and broader bandwidths. An 6-layer design provides more degrees of freedom than 6-layer, allowing for better flattening of the reflectance curve across the visible spectrum and wider angles.
expected_advantages: Potentially superior angular stability due to high index contrast.
MgF2 outer layer is chemically durable.
known_risks: TiO2 can be sensitive to deposition conditions (stoichiometry affects index).
Potential for higher sensitivity to thickness errors due to more layers.

research_influence: Evidence from s2-chunk:CorpusId:283155301 influenced the choice of using a 4-layer LHLH structure as a baseline and highlighted the importance of minimum thickness constraints (>10 nm) for fabricability.

Evidence from s2-chunk:CorpusId:284130796 supported the inclusion of robustness analysis (angle and thickness errors) as a critical part of the evaluation, mirroring their sensitivity study methodology.
Evidence from s2-chunk:CorpusId:270586583 motivated the use of SiO2/MgF2 and other low/high index pairs, confirming their effectiveness for broadband AR on glass substrates.
Evidence from s2-chunk:CorpusId:120897377 provided context on the use of Ta2O5 and TiO2, supporting their inclusion in the candidate material set for high-index layers.
unresolved_decisions: Whether to start the stack with a low-index or high-index material is left to the optimizer in routes 03 and 04, but fixed in routes 01 and 02 for comparison. Route 01 starts with Low, Route 02 starts with Low. Route 03 starts with Low (SiO2). Route 04 starts with Low (MgF2). This consistency allows for fair comparison of layer count and material pair effects.
The exact weighting of 'fewer layers' vs 'lower thickness' vs 'performance' is handled by the TMM task compiler's ranking logic, as these are soft objectives.
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: Stop after the bounded route portfolio is exhausted or further search stagnates. Return every physically verified candidate and report soft objective trade-offs without a performance admission threshold.
